sources.title: Horse-race Java fixture and actual-candidate independent stress oracle

claims.text: The preserved source requires ten simulated horse threads, a global ready-before-start condition and a global finished-before-announcement condition; it does not require a specific synchronizer.
The three-latch implementation reports ready before awaiting start, the referee opens start only after ready reaches zero, and the referee announces only after finish reaches zero.
finish is decremented from finally and actual-candidate failure stress terminates within the bounded timeout while preserving the failure as an exception.
ConcurrentLinkedQueue supplies a concurrent scoring container and the answer explicitly defines insertion as the observable scoring point before the final result snapshot.

boundary_tests.case: actual candidate action-release stress across 100 rounds
boundary_tests.expected: all ten actions cross start gate and produce ten unique results

findings: The exact repository source requires ten horse threads, no start until every horse is ready, and no referee announcement until every horse reaches the terminal phase; it does not mandate CountDownLatch or any other specific synchronizer.
The candidate keeps the tool choice answer-side and separates ready aggregation, one-shot start broadcast and finish aggregation into three latches with distinct directions.
The ordering avoids the classic logical deadlock: each horse reports ready before awaiting start, while the referee awaits all ready before opening start.
finish.countDown is in finally, so action failure cannot strand the referee completion wait; the failure is separately recorded and rethrown rather than reported as a normal result.
The writer telemetry fixture verifies source ordering over 60 rounds, while an independently authored test compiles and executes the actual candidate for 100 rounds and a bounded failure case.
The answer defines the observable finishOrder.add operation as the simulation scoring point instead of claiming an unobservable absolute physical finishing order.
No project experience is fabricated; timeout, DNF, repeated-race and thread-pool policies remain explicitly outside the preserved source contract.
